chain.g: to find; to acquire, attain, get, hold, receive
to find; to hold; to seize; to take

ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *gʰe(n)d-der. Proto-Indo-European *gʰed-eti Proto-Germanic *getaną Old Norse getabor. Middle English geten English get From Middle English geten, from Old Norse geta, from Proto-Germanic *getaną (“to find; to acquire, attain, get, hold, receive”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰed- (“to find; to hold; to seize; to take”).
Variant of git.
Sumerian 𒁍der. Sumerian 𒁍𒁕bor. Akkadian 𒁍𒁕der.? Hebrew גֵּט (gēṭ)der. English get From Hebrew גֵּט (gēṭ).

senses.d: To obtain; to acquire.
ex: I'm going to get a computer tomorrow from the discount store.
Lance is going to get Mary a ring.

senses.d: To receive.
ex: I got a computer from my parents for my birthday.
He got a severe reprimand for that.

senses.d: To have. See usage notes.
ex: I've got a concert ticket for you.
"Yeah, and I got a bridge in Brooklyn I'd like to sell you," was Peter's response to his wife.

senses.d: To fetch, bring, take.
ex: Can you get my bag from the living-room, please?
I need to get this to the office.

senses.d: To become, or cause oneself to become (often with temporary states, past participle adjectives and comparatives).
ex: Near-synonyms: become, turn, go, come, fall, grow, wax
I'm getting hungry; how about you?

senses.d: To cause to become; to bring about.
ex: That song gets me so depressed every time I hear it.
I'll get this finished by lunchtime.

senses.d: To cause to do.
ex: Somehow she got him to agree to it.
I can't get it to work.

senses.d: To cause to come or go or move.
ex: I got him to his room.
Get thee behind me.

senses.d: To adopt, assume, arrive at, or progress towards (a certain position, location, state).
ex: The actors are getting into position.
When are we going to get to London?

senses.d: To cover (a certain distance) while travelling.
ex: to get a mile

senses.d: Offspring, especially illegitimate.
ex: You must admit that the bastard get of Paul Atreides would be no more than juicy morsels for those two [tigers].
‘You were a high lord's get. Don't tell me Lord Eddard Stark of Winterfell never killed a man.’

senses.d: Lineage.
A difficult return or block of a shot.
Something gotten, something gained or won; an acquisition.
ex: I had reconnected with the lust of my life while landing a big get for the magazine.

senses.d: A message or post on an online platform, particularly imageboards, with a unique identifier deemed special or rare, usually due to patterns in the ID.
Synonym of git (“contemptible person”).
ex: Kylie: Oi, Bono! You lazy get! Have you finished my song yet?

senses.d: A Jewish writ of divorce.
ex: In Israel, rabbinic courts can imprison men until they acquiesce and grant gets to their wives.
